newsitem.title: UK: UK building societies bill passes House of Commons.
newsitem.headline: UK building societies bill passes House of Commons.

text.p: The Building Societies bill cleared its remaining stages in Britain's lower House of Commons on Monday without a formal vote.
The bill, which enjoys all-party support, must clear the upper House of Lords and then return to the Commons before it can become law.

With only three days remaining before parliament ends for the May 1 general election, government and opposition business managers must decide whether to allocate scarce legislative time to ensure passage of the bill.

The bill, which has cross-party support, would remove certain restrictions on mutually owned building societies, allowing them to compete more effectively with societies that convert to banks with the status of public limited companies.
A senior Labour official said the bill did not go far enough but the main opposition party could live with it and hoped it would become law before the election.

He said Labour had refrained from putting down amendments in order to facilitate the bill's passage and to reduce the risk that ministers opposed to the measure, led by Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine, would try to scupper it.
Economic Secretary Angela Knight and her Labour "shadow", Mike O'Brien, were expected to hold talks to work out how the bill could be handled in the House of Lords.
